ticket: On Airflow below 3.3, durable=None is treated as if durable was set. Repro: write an operator on the common.compat ResumableJobMixin and construct it with durable=None. Actual: mypy reports an incompatible type for durable=None, and at runtime the operator warns '`durable` has no effect on Airflow versions below 3.3.' although nothing was set. Expected: durable=None means not set (no warning, no type error); leaving durable out stays silent; an explicit durable=True/False still warns on Airflow below 3.3; and a non-bool value such as durable="yes" is still a type error.

MSGraphSensor never times out. Repro: an MSGraphSensor with timeout=300 and retry_delay=30, pointed at a Graph request whose response never reports done. Actual: the sensor keeps polling well past 5 minutes, indefinitely, so soft_fail=True and never_fail never take effect. Separately, a hung Graph request can wait up to 7 days before failing. Expected: once timeout seconds have passed since the try started, the task fails with AirflowSensorTimeout (or is skipped with soft_fail), and no single Graph request outlives the sensor's timeout.

Uploading many files in one request can stall the server. Repro: an endpoint taking files: list[UploadFile] = File(), and one multipart POST carrying several thousand small files while other requests are in flight on the same worker. Actual (reported to the maintainer by email; not reproduced locally): while that request's form is processed, the event loop is flooded with pending work, one item per uploaded file, and other requests on the worker slow down. Expected: handling one request's uploads keeps the event loop responsive however many files the request carries, and uploads are still fully read before the endpoint runs.

FastAPI does not work on the oldest Pydantic its dependency range allows. Repro: install FastAPI with pydantic==2.7.0 (the pin is pydantic>=2.7.0) and run the test suite. Actual: AttributeError: Config has no attribute 'val_json_bytes'. With Pydantic 2.9 and 2.10, the OpenAPI schema tests for schema compatibility and for discriminated union bodies fail because the generated schema differs from the expected one (additionalProperties). CI's minimum-versions job did not catch this because it was not installing the oldest allowed Pydantic. Expected: the declared Pydantic range is honest, and the test suite passes on every Pydantic version inside it, oldest and newest.

Server-sent events corrupt data that ends in a newline. Repro: an endpoint with response_class=EventSourceResponse that yields ServerSentEvent(data="Hello
") (or raw_data="Hello
"). Actual: the stream carries b'data: Hello

'; the trailing newline is lost, so the client receives "Hello" instead of "Hello
". The same happens to comments. Separately, a payload containing a vertical tab, form feed, \x85 or U+2028 arrives at the client as two data fields. Seen on FastAPI 0.135.3 and 0.136.1, Python 3.12. Expected: the client receives exactly the string the endpoint sent, including trailing newlines and those characters, as the SSE spec defines.

Memory usage rises sharply after upgrading from FastAPI 0.120.4. Repro: an app with a chain of 100 dependencies, each one Depends on the next, and endpoints whose signatures take many Depends(...) parameters on that chain; compare resident memory on 0.120.4 and on 0.121.3 or later. Actual: a production app that ran under 400 MB on 0.120.4 is killed out of memory on 0.121.3, and every release up to 0.128 shows the same growth. Expected: memory use for the same app stays close to 0.120.4.

Large apps lose the speed-up from the recent dependency memory reduction (#16049). Repro: an app with more than 1,024 distinct dependency functions; compare per-request time against an app with a few hundred. Actual: users report that apps with over 1,024 dependency functions see per-request dependency overhead return, while small apps are unaffected. Expected: apps with a few thousand distinct dependency functions get the same per-request dependency performance as small apps, without a noticeable memory cost.
